_comment: A ratchet, not a target. The gate fails when coverage drops BELOW these
numbers; it never fails for being above them, and it does not raise itself.
Raising is deliberate: a floor that follows the last run turns one lucky
commit into a permanent obligation and teaches people to switch the gate off.
RE-BASELINED 2026-09-07 for vitest 5 / @vitest/coverage-v8 5, and the reason
matters more than the numbers: THE INSTRUMENT CHANGED, the coverage did not.
Same 1050 tests, same sources, measured by both:
vitest 2 / v8 2         vitest 5 / v8 5
The COVERED counts went UP in every category (3413->3593 branches,
444->698 functions). What moved is what the tool counts as coverable:
+616 branches and +323 functions it did not see before. Percentages across
a major version of the provider are not comparable, and reading the branch
figure as a 6.5-point regression would be wrong.
So these are set at the new measurement rounded down, exactly as the
previous set was on 2026-09-05 (84/79/93/84 against the old instrument).
A future drop against THESE is a real drop.
Earlier history: the August figure was 75.4% statements with prompt_loop.ts
at 50.1%; the jump to the 2026-09-05 numbers was partly real tests and
partly the removal of agent.ts, 339 lines that nothing called.
